steps.prompt: A ball dropped from $16$ m bounces back to half its height each time. How high is the 4th bounce? Do you think the total distance it travels is finite?

cards.title: Same ratio every time
cards.body: A geometric sequence multiplies by the same ratio $r$ each time: $a, ar, ar^2, \ldots$ Term number $n$ is $ar^{n - 1}$. Find $r$ by dividing a term by the one before it. The middle of three terms in a row is the geometric mean: $b^2 = ac$.

steps.text: Term $8$ is $3 \times 2^{7} = 3 \times 128 = 384$: seven multiplications after the first term.

cards.title: Geometric sums
cards.body: The sum of $n$ terms is $a \cdot \frac{r^n - 1}{r - 1}$. For example, $1 + 2 + 4 + \cdots + 2^{n} = 2^{n + 1} - 1$. When $-1 < r < 1$ the terms shrink and the sum FOREVER is $\frac{a}{1 - r}$.

cards.title: Worked example: a sum that never ends

steps.text: $a = 12$ and each term is half the one before, so $r = \frac{1}{2}$.

cards.title: The common trap: one power too many
cards.body: Term $n$ uses $r^{n - 1}$, not $r^n$. $1 + r + \cdots + r^{n}$ has $n + 1$ terms. The forever sum only works when $-1 < r < 1$. And a negative ratio makes the signs alternate.

prompts: Why does $12 + 6 + 3 + \cdots$ add up to a finite number, but $1 + 2 + 4 + \cdots$ doesn't?
